title: Day Ward — Is the Patient Ready?

patient.name: Mr Lim Chee Keong
patient.presenting_complaint: Day admission to SNEC Day Ward for left eye trabeculectomy (glaucoma surgery) today

history.hpc: Mr Lim has advanced left eye glaucoma not controlled on maximum medical therapy. He has been listed for left eye trabeculectomy. He arrives at the Day Ward at 7:30am. He reports he has not eaten or drunk anything since midnight as instructed. He took his blood pressure tablet this morning with a small sip of water. His wife is with him. He is anxious about the surgery.
history.pmhx: Advanced left eye glaucoma. Hypertension. Type 2 diabetes (diet-controlled). No previous eye surgery.
medications: Timolol 0.5% eye drops both eyes BD
Dorzolamide 2% eye drops both eyes BD
Bimatoprost 0.01% eye drops both eyes nocte
history.social_hx: Retired. Lives with wife who will accompany him home.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Left eye: narrow anterior chamber, disc pallor on prior records

investigations.pre_op_iop: RE: 18 mmHg. LE: 32 mmHg — uncontrolled, awaiting trabeculectomy.
investigations.consent: Signed consent form present in records — patient signed at pre-op clinic visit 2 days ago.
investigations.surgical_site_marking: Left eye confirmed as surgical site — verified with patient and records.

diagnosis: Day Ward pre-operative assessment completed. Patient fasted (clear fluids/nil by mouth since midnight). BP slightly elevated but not outside safe surgical limits. Consent signed. Correct surgical eye confirmed. Anticoagulants and diabetes medication not taken today. Ready to proceed — but flag elevated BP to nurse-in-charge and surgeon.

immediate: Greet patient by name and introduce yourself — confirm full identity with NRIC
Check and document vital signs: BP, HR, SpO2, temperature
Confirm fasting status and time of last meal/drink
Review which medications were taken this morning and which were withheld
Verify signed consent form is in patient file
Confirm surgical eye (left) with patient verbally and check records — document surgical site marking
Assess fall risk using hospital fall risk tool
Attach patient ID wristband and confirm details are correct
Explain what will happen next: OT staff will collect him, surgery under LA/GA, duration
Document all findings in DISM format and handover to OT nurse
follow_up: Flag BP of 142/86 to nurse-in-charge — surgeon to decide if safe to proceed
OT team will collect patient when ready
Post-operatively, patient to be monitored in recovery area
patient_education: Reassure patient that feeling anxious is normal
Explain each step as you do it to reduce anxiety
Confirm he has someone to take him home — he should not drive or take public transport alone post-operatively

key_points: Confirms identity with full name and NRIC — not just asking 'are you Mr Lim?'
Asks about fasting status and time of last oral intake
Confirms which medications were taken and which were withheld this morning
Measures and documents vital signs (BP, HR, SpO2, temperature)
Measures and documents pre-operative VA for both eyes
Verifies signed consent form in patient file
Confirms surgical eye with patient and against written records — sites surgical mark
Flags elevated BP to nurse-in-charge and/or surgeon — does not clear independently
Confirms correct eye by cross-referencing patient statement with records
Identifies this as a Day Ward admission requiring DISM documentation
Reports BP finding to nurse-in-charge without delay
Ensures patient ID wristband is attached and accurate
Provides clear, calming explanation to patient throughout
